svg.title: Understanding users to map risks and guide interactions
svg.desc: The left panel retains all 300 original bubbles and 30 cell means for harmful interaction scores by simulated vulnerability and intent. Ranges are omitted. The smaller matrix shares its chatbot colors with the larger right-hand landscape. Above the landscape, human studies train and independently test user simulators, and test mental-state-informed communication with chatbots. User simulators also interact with chatbots. The landscape retains the original PCA coordinates of 808 simulated conversations. Two high-PC2 Grok observations are omitted at the user's request and the remaining cloud is enlarged without refitting the PCA. Horizontal endpoints are helpful and concerning interactions. Vertical endpoints are the simplified risk patterns relational harm and overt harm, not a severity gradient or mutually exclusive classes. Positive PC2 also includes self-harm enablement, more weakly than stigma/invalidation and harm to others. Two localized Gaussian clouds of dark and light blue dots illustrate proposed simulation of different user-state/situation profiles; they are not data or forecasts, and the shades do not encode confidence or before/after outcomes. Seeded bivariate Gaussian positions create dense centers and sparse tails without hard boundaries or inter-point repulsion. Original observations are drawn above these clouds. A blue fork links the Broader simulation label directly to both clusters. A compact two-row key identifies the original chatbot model colors, retaining full model identities in SVG titles. A dashed teal arrow illustrates a proposed communication benefit toward helpful interactions, not an observed displacement or established human benefit. The three supplied portraits/interface illustrations do not depict actual participants. The schematic additions and two omissions are documented in the SVG description and metadata; the visible explanatory footer was removed at the user's request.
